title: AC-MT201-AnnotationRecordSchema

scope.summary:
GOAL: Define the SINGLE shared annotation record schema `hsk.annotation@1` as pure Rust types + a committed JSON Schema, used identically by human (operator) and model authors — provenance fields, not separate schemas, distinguish the two. This is the root type of the whole AC family: MT-202 anchors plug into it, MT-203 persists it, MT-205/206 transport it, and future Studio/Stage surfaces adopt it through the MT-208 seam.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) new module src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/ with mod.rs (module docs + re-exports + AnnotationError) and record.rs (all record types); (b) committed JSON Schema file src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/schema/hsk_annotation_v1.schema.json kept in sync by a round-trip test; (c) one `pub mod annotations;` line added to src/backend/handshake_core/src/lib.rs; (d) unit tests. NO storage, NO routes, NO re-anchoring logic in this MT.

DETAILED SPEC — record `Annotation` (serde Serialize/Deserialize, deny_unknown_fields):
1. `schema: String` — always "hsk.annotation@1" (serde default + validation).
2. `id: uuid::Uuid`, `workspace_id: uuid::Uuid`.
3. `subject: AnnotationSubject` — enum (tagged, `kind` discriminator) describing WHAT is annotated: `File { path: String }` (live file in the workspace), `Diff { old_ref: String, new_ref: String, path: String }` (a comparison between two content refs, e.g. worktree-merge review), `ProseBlock { document_id: Uuid, block_id: Uuid }` (rich/knowledge document block; consumed by the PD family MT-241+). Optional field on all variants: `mt_run_ref: Option<String>` — free-form reference to an MT run/mt_signal correlation id (MT-121 seam, string-typed on purpose so this crate does not import orchestration types).
4. `anchor_ref: AnchorRef` — in THIS MT a schema-versioned opaque envelope `AnchorRef { anchor_version: u32, value: serde_json::Value }`; MT-202 replaces the payload with the typed `AnnotationAnchor` while keeping the serialized shape stable (anchor_version stays the outer discriminator). Document this handoff in record.rs module docs.
5. `body: String` — markdown. Empty body is REJECTED at construction (typed error), max length 64 KiB (typed error beyond).
6. `kind: AnnotationKind` — enum comment | suggestion | finding | question (serde lowercase).
7. `thread: Option<Uuid>` — `parent_annotation_id` for replies; None = thread root. Replies inherit subject/anchor from the root (the reply record still carries its own copies for self-containment; constructor helper `Annotation::reply_to(&parent, ...)` copies them).
8. `state: AnnotationState` — enum open | resolved | orphaned | outdated (serde lowercase). New records are always `open`; only MT-203 store transitions (resolve/reopen) and the MT-204 re-anchor engine (orphaned/outdated) may change it.
9. `author: AnnotationAuthor` — struct { kind: AuthorKind (operator | model), display: String, provenance: Option<ModelProvenance> }. `ModelProvenance { robot_id: String, session_id: String, run_id: String }` — MANDATORY when kind == model, FORBIDDEN when kind == operator. This is the Gerrit RobotCommentInfo hardening over hunk's free-form `author` string: a model annotation without robot_id + session_id + run_id must be UNREPRESENTABLE through the constructor and REJECTED by a custom Deserialize validation (implement via `#[serde(try_from)]` or a validating `TryFrom<RawAnnotationAuthor>`).
10. `fix_suggestions: Vec<FixSuggestion>` — Gerrit fix_suggestions shape: `FixSuggestion { description: String, replacements: Vec<FixReplacement> }`, `FixReplacement { path: String, range: ReplacementRange, replacement: String }`, `ReplacementRange { start_line: u32, start_char: u32, end_line: u32, end_char: u32 }` (0-based, half-open, UTF-8 byte columns — documented in rustdoc). Typically model-authored; allowed empty for plain comments.
11. `created_at_utc: chrono OR time RFC3339 string` — use whichever datetime representation the existing handshake_core storage records use (inspect src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/knowledge.rs for the incumbent convention and MATCH it); `updated_at_utc` same type, equal to created_at_utc on creation.
12. `AnnotationError` enum in mod.rs with typed variants: EmptyBody, BodyTooLarge, MissingModelProvenance, ProvenanceOnOperatorAuthor, SchemaMismatch, InvalidAnchorEnvelope — all `thiserror`-derived if thiserror is already a workspace dep (verify; otherwise manual Display impls).
13. JSON Schema: commit hsk_annotation_v1.schema.json describing the full record (draft 2020-12). A unit test deserializes the schema file, serializes a maximal sample Annotation, and asserts every serialized key is declared by the schema (drift tripwire in BOTH directions: schema keys not producible by the types also fail).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/knowledge.rs and src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/knowledge_documents.rs (wtc-native-editors-v1 worktree) to copy the incumbent id/timestamp/serde conventions — do NOT invent new ones.
2. Create src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/mod.rs with module docs stating the seam law: this module must never import editor/notes/document modules (enforced by MT-208); it may import only std, serde, uuid, the workspace datetime crate, and thiserror.
3. Create record.rs with the types above, constructors `Annotation::new_operator(...)`, `Annotation::new_model(...)` (provenance required by signature), `Annotation::reply_to(...)`, and validating deserialization.
4. Write hsk_annotation_v1.schema.json by hand (or via a dev-only schemars generation run committed as a static file — do NOT add schemars as a runtime dep).
5. Unit tests: serde round-trip for every enum variant combination; model-author-without-provenance rejected on both construct and deserialize; operator-author-with-provenance rejected; empty/oversized body rejected; reply_to copies subject + anchor and sets thread; schema drift tripwire test.
6. Wire `pub mod annotations;` into lib.rs; run proof targets.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (GUI owned by NA family MT-221+)
acceptance_criteria: hsk.annotation@1 record types exist in src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/record.rs with exactly the specified fields: id, workspace_id, subject, anchor_ref, body, kind, thread, state, author, fix_suggestions, created/updated timestamps, schema tag.

A model-authored annotation without robot_id + session_id + run_id is unrepresentable via constructors AND rejected by deserialization with the typed MissingModelProvenance error; an operator-authored annotation carrying provenance is rejected with ProvenanceOnOperatorAuthor.
One shared schema serves human and model authors — no second record type, no parallel model-only schema (grep-provable: exactly one `struct Annotation` in the annotations module).
AnnotationSubject covers File, Diff, and ProseBlock targets with an optional string-typed mt_run_ref on each (MT-121 seam without an orchestration import).
fix_suggestions serialize in the Gerrit-style description + replacements[{path, range, replacement}] shape with 0-based half-open ranges documented in rustdoc.
hsk_annotation_v1.schema.json is committed and the bidirectional schema-drift tripwire test passes.
AnchorRef is a versioned opaque envelope whose serialized shape MT-202 can replace without breaking round-trips (documented handoff note in record.rs).
cargo build -p handshake_core succeeds; the annotations module imports nothing from knowledge_document, knowledge_wiki, loom_*, atelier, or any api/storage module.
proof_targets: cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml annotation_record -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'
grep -c 'pub struct Annotation ' src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/record.rs | grep -q '^1$' (single shared record type)
grep -rn 'use crate::\(knowledge\|loom\|atelier\|api\|storage\)' src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/ | wc -l | grep -q '^0$' (seam law pre-check ahead of MT-208 enforcement)
implementation_notes: Research basis (packet-level, operator-verified 2026-07-21): concept from modem-dev/hunk agent-context sidecar (annotations with summary/rationale/author), hardened with the Gerrit CommentInfo/RobotCommentInfo model — hunk's free-form `author` string is explicitly INSUFFICIENT provenance; Gerrit's robot_id/robot_run_id extension fields are the adopted fix (mapped here to robot_id/session_id/run_id).

Single-schema decision: Gerrit robot comments EXTEND the human comment schema rather than forking it; Handshake adopts the same shape so every downstream surface (store, routes, tools, GUI, Studio/Stage) handles one type.
The AnchorRef opaque-envelope indirection exists ONLY so MT-201 has no dependency; MT-202 owns the typed anchor. Do not sneak anchor semantics (quote, context, hash) into this MT.
Datetime + uuid conventions MUST be copied from the incumbent storage records (storage/knowledge.rs) — mismatched conventions here would force MT-203 into conversion shims.
Keep the module free of tokio/async and of any DB type: pure data + validation, synchronously testable, so MT-208 can prove Studio/Stage adoption with zero runtime baggage.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/core schema MT; operator GUI surfaces for annotations are owned by the NA family (MT-221+).

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal data-model MT with no operator-visible behavior yet; the UserManual entries land with the MT-205 routes and MT-206 tool surface.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FlightRecorder: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — pure type/schema module emits no runtime events; event emission starts at the MT-203 store (EventLedger receipts) and MT-204 engine (MT-161 FR kinds).
internal_diagnostics: WIRED — all validation failures are typed AnnotationError variants (no stringly errors, no silent coercion), surfaced by every downstream consumer.
Palmistry: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — no long-running runtime posture; pure data types.
risk_if_missed: Without a single hardened record schema every downstream MT invents its own annotation shape: model annotations land with hunk-style free-form authorship (no provenance, unattributable in a multi-agent swarm), human and model comments fork into incompatible types, and Studio/Stage adoption of the seam becomes a migration instead of an import.

risks: RISK-1: Model provenance enforced only in the constructor — a crafted JSON payload deserializes a model annotation with no robot_id/session_id/run_id, and swarm attribution silently degrades to hunk's free-form-author weakness.
RISK-2: The JSON Schema file drifts from the Rust types (field added to one, not the other) and external consumers (sidecar import/export, future Studio) validate against a stale contract.
RISK-3: A downstream MT finds the shared type inconvenient and forks a model-only annotation struct, splitting the human/model surface the whole design exists to unify.
RISK-4: Anchor semantics leak into MT-201 (e.g. quote or hash fields on the record), pre-empting the MT-202 typed anchor and forcing a breaking re-serialization later.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Provenance validation runs in Deserialize (try_from), not only in constructors; a dedicated negative test feeds raw JSON with kind=model and no provenance and asserts the typed rejection.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): The bidirectional schema-drift tripwire test fails when either the serialized record produces a key the schema does not declare or the schema declares a key the types cannot produce.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Acceptance criterion pins exactly one `struct Annotation` (grep proof target); MT-208's seam consumer example re-proves single-type adoption.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): AnchorRef is an opaque versioned envelope in this MT; the grep proof over annotations/ shows no quote/context/hash identifiers before MT-202.

research_provenance.source: Operator-verified annotation research 2026-07-21: modem-dev/hunk (github.com/modem-dev/hunk, MIT, ~7.5k stars) agent-context sidecar concept with author-as-free-form-string identified as insufficient provenance; Gerrit CommentInfo/RobotCommentInfo (robot_id, robot_run_id, fix_suggestions[{description, replacements:[{path, range, replacement}]}]) adopted as the hardened shared human+model schema; REJECTED: git-notes storage (commit granularity, orphaning) and reusing hunk TS code (concept only). Grounding audit of wtc-native-editors-v1: src/backend/handshake_core/src/lib.rs module list (annotations is a new top-level module), storage/knowledge.rs + api/knowledge_documents.rs incumbent id/timestamp/receipt conventions.
corrections: hunk live-comment targets (exactly one of hunk|hunkNumber|oldLine|newLine) are deliberately NOT adopted at the record level — targeting lives entirely in the MT-202 anchor model; the record only carries the versioned anchor envelope.
Gerrit robot_run_id is split into session_id + run_id to match Handshake's session/run identity model used by the CS family and FR correlation (string-typed, no orchestration import).
